title: Attention Mathematics: Q, K, V and Softmax
summary: A step-by-step view of scaled dot-product attention: project token representations into queries, keys and values; score query-key compatibility; normalize with softmax; then mix values.
eli5: Each token asks a question with its query, compares that question with every token's key, and uses the resulting weights to blend the information stored in the values.

sections.heading: Three learned projections
sections.expression: Q = XW_Q,   K = XW_K,   V = XW_V
sections.explanation: The same input representations X are projected through different learned matrices. Queries are used to ask what is relevant, keys are used for matching, and values contain the information that will be mixed.
sections.shapes: For n tokens with model width d_model: X is n×d_model. A head commonly produces Q,K,V with shape n×d_k or n×d_v.

sections.heading: Compatibility scores
sections.explanation: Every query is dotted with every key. Dividing by √dₖ keeps score magnitudes better behaved as the vector dimension grows, which helps softmax avoid becoming excessively sharp during optimization.
sections.shapes: Q is n×dₖ and Kᵀ is dₖ×n, so S is n×n.

sections.heading: Normalize and mix
sections.explanation: Softmax is applied across the candidate keys for each query. Each row of A becomes a set of weights that sums to one. Multiplying A by V returns a weighted mixture of value vectors for every token.

sections.heading: A two-key example
sections.intro: Use one query q = [1,0], keys k₁ = [1,0], k₂ = [0,1], and values v₁ = [2,0], v₂ = [0,2]. Let dₖ = 2.
steps: Dot products are q·k₁ = 1 and q·k₂ = 0.
sections.result: The output leans toward v₁ because k₁ matched the query more strongly.

sections.heading: Causal masking in a decoder LLM
sections.body: During autoregressive language modeling, a token must not use information from future tokens. A causal mask makes disallowed future attention scores effectively negative infinity before softmax, so their normalized weights become zero.

sections.heading: Why multiple heads?
sections.body: Multi-head attention runs several learned Q/K/V projections in parallel and concatenates their outputs. Different heads can learn different compatibility patterns. A head is not guaranteed to correspond to a clean human-interpretable rule; it is simply a separately parameterized attention subspace.

sections.heading: Attention is not a database lookup
sections.body: The query/key/value analogy is useful, but ordinary soft attention computes differentiable weighted mixtures rather than retrieving one exact record. High attention weight also should not automatically be interpreted as a complete causal explanation of the model's decision.

sections.heading: Check yourself
sections.question: Why does QKᵀ have an n×n shape for n tokens?
sections.answer: Because every one of the n query vectors is compared with every one of the n key vectors, producing one compatibility score for each query-key pair.
